html:
Thrace is the region of southeast Europe between the Balkan Mountains, the Aegean and the Black Sea, home in ancient times to the Thracians. The map shows the label in 1500, 1000 and 700 BCE, before the Thracians appear in writing.

The Thracians were many Indo-European tribes who spoke related languages and shared customs but rarely united. Herodotus wrote that they were the most numerous people after the Indians and would be unbeatable if they had one ruler. They were farmers and horse breeders, known to the Greeks as fierce warriors. Their nobles were buried under mounds with rich gold and silver; the Valley of the Thracian Kings near Kazanlak in Bulgaria holds many such tombs. The singer Orpheus of Greek myth was said to be Thracian.

From the 600s BCE Greeks founded colonies on the Thracian coast. The Persians under Darius conquered part of the region about 513 BCE. In the 400s BCE the Odrysian kingdom united many tribes, until Philip II of Macedon subdued it. Rome made Thrace a province in 46 CE. The most famous Thracian is the gladiator Spartacus, who led a slave revolt against Rome in 73 BCE.
